messages:
leah: Opening a docs PR to consolidate invoke patterns + parsing heuristics, and do a link sweep for outdated examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4823 — can y'all take a quick pass?

omar: On it, thanks. I'll check SDK snippets (python/js) for function-calling examples.

ryan: Can we add a tiny "robust parse" example? I've seen nested arrays break naive parsers. Show `nullable` + `oneOf` fallback pattern.

leah: Yes — plan is: add a compact JSON Schema snippet, a fallback parse example, and a short guardrail section recommending explicit enums for action types.

docs-bot: link-checker ran on the branch — 3 broken example links found, auto-commented on the PR.

sophia: Quick note: in the JS snippet use `redwood.callTool({ name, input })` instead of the old `invoke` alias. Less confusing for new SDK users.

omar: Good call. I'll update the python snippet to show `client.call_tool(...)` and include a small test harness:\n```\n# parse fallback (python)\ntry:\n    out = json.loads(resp_text)\nexcept JSONDecodeError:\n    # small heuristic fallback\n    out = fallback_regex_parse(resp_text)\n```\n
ryan: +1 on the harness. Also add a 2-sentence note about streaming responses and token splits affecting parseability — we've had a few support threads about that.

leah: I'll draft both the streaming note and the JSON fallback section. Tagging @sophia for the JS change and @omar for python. Aiming to merge EOD tomorrow. Any objections?

sophia: None. I'll run a quick lint pass after you push.

omar: Looks good. I'll also open a follow-up issue to track missing snippet translations for Private docs (VPC/on-prem).

leah: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
